scope: Follow-on bounded static candidate trace and disposable ordering experiments. No behavior change or native parity is claimed.

nativeStatic.method: Read-only Ghidra 12.1.4 import with automatic analysis disabled; disassemble and decompile the three call targets observed in candidate 0x14032c400.
observations: Candidate 0x14032e330 uses a four-byte FNV-style lookup for an integer key. Its decompilation walks records, searches three integer slots for a key and appends the following two cyclic slots as a pair.
Candidate 0x14032c400 calls 0x14032edf0 for both values of a returned pair and conditionally calls 0x14032dae0; the data structures and geometry semantics are not established.

applicationExperiments.observation: None of these local ordering variants matches all native outputs. No variant was applied to production.

limitations: Candidate static paths and record types remain unbound to the observed native Split operation.
Three manufactured examples do not establish general triangulation behavior. Exact native parity and M2 closure remain open.

additionalPointOrderExperiments.scope: Disposable shared-kernel ordering experiments, not production changes or native path proof
additionalPointOrderExperiments.result: Nine candidate orderings based on barycentric sums, differences and distances did not match all three native controls. Best aggregate matches varied by case; none was applied.

distancePivotExperiment.scope: Disposable crossed-strip prototype using closest or farthest point-to-segment pivot; not a faithful native implementation or production code.
distancePivotExperiment.interpretation: A deliberate throw showed that at least one crossed strip was reached. A second run deliberately throwing for any successfully constructed strip with a chain longer than three vertices passed all three controls. Thus the prototype did not exercise a choice between multiple interior pivot candidates on these controls, so identical results cannot support or refute the native distance-pivot hypothesis. Further work needs an input with a nontrivial chain and a live native binding.
limitations: The deliberate throw run failed as intended and cleaned up; the other instrumented run passed. Neither verifies native behavior.
The scratch prototype does not check every polygon validity condition and must not be used in production.

nontrivialControl.observation: A deterministic synthetic face and four intersecting segments reached a constructed strip with chain lengths 4 and 3. On this input, nearest-pivot and baseline produced 17 matching unordered facets and passed positive winding and total area checks. The farthest-pivot prototype failed a later constraint recovery. The runner itself exited zero because it records child exit codes, so its passing guard is cleanup evidence, not a pass for both variants. Neither candidate has been compared to a native export.
